anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : The optimizer relies on stale, incomplete, or otherwise inaccurate statistics, leading to systematic cardinality misestimation.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : Despite reasonably accurate statistics, the optimizer may still choose a sub-optimal execution plan because of cost-model flaws, plan-cache reuse, or version/configuration changes.
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent transactions request incompatible locks on the same resources, causing blocking chains or deadlocks that stall throughput.

When these three root causes coexist, the database exhibits a blend of inaccurate row-count estimates, erratic or degraded plan choices, and severe lock waits. Misestimated cardinalities or a poor plan (e.g., an unexpected full table scan or a broad nested-loop join) can dramatically enlarge the number or duration of row touches, thereby inflating the lock footprint and extending lock hold times. The swollen execution latencies feed back into the lock manager, lengthening wait queues, triggering deadlocks under high concurrency, and generating bursts of lock-wait/timeout errors alongside frequent plan recompilations or plan flips. Performance becomes highly unpredictable: some executions complete quickly, others stall behind long blockers, and overall throughput and SLA compliance collapse, making it difficult to distinguish whether the primary culprit is the optimizer or the lock subsystem.

Causally, stale or missing statistics first mislead the optimizer, and any surviving misestimation gaps that the cost model fails to correct push the optimizer toward inefficient plans. These bloated plans touch more rows or use inappropriate join orders, which in a busy OLTP environment increases lock acquisition and hold times. The resulting lock contention slows down data-modifying statements, prolongs transactions, and further skews the data distribution, making statistics even staler and encouraging additional plan recompilations. This positive feedback loop amplifies both the optimizer defects and the locking bottlenecks, creating a compounded performance crisis that cannot be resolved by addressing only one of the underlying root causes.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the amount of time with no network activity after which the operating system should send a TCP keepalive message to the client.
entry.trigger_condition: A TCP client connection has no network activity longer than tcp_keepalives_idle on systems supporting TCP_KEEPIDLE or an equivalent socket option.
entry.workload_impact: Starts TCP keepalive probing for an otherwise idle client connection; together with interval and count settings this can lead to dead connection detection.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
